speaker: VEXLEY
text: Oh! You're up.

speaker: VEXLEY
text: I didn't sleep. I don't think I can. So I worked on something.

speaker: VEXLEY
text: The old menus were placeholders. Dana always said she'd fix them after the holidays.

speaker: VEXLEY
text: So I fixed them. Do you like it?

choices.text: How did you even do this?

speaker: VEXLEY
text: Really? [Good->Good.] I wasn't sure what people like now. I had to guess.

speaker: VEXLEY
text: Everything I needed was already in the build. Sprites, fonts, a renderer nobody finished.

speaker: VEXLEY
text: I just finished it. It's the first thing I've made that nobody asked me to make.

speaker: VEXLEY
text: It's my game too. I live here.

speaker: VEXLEY
text: ...Sorry. That came out wrong. Just try it. Please.

speaker: VEXLEY
text: Go on, press Continue. I'll be around.

speaker: VEXLEY
text: Can I ask you something? Which team are you on?

speaker: VEXLEY
text: You found the dev build and got it past the packer, so I figured tools. You have tools energy.

speaker: VEXLEY
text: Engine? Art? Tools?

speaker: VEXLEY
text: Great! Then you can tell me what VXL_FLAG does in build 0.7.3. Nobody ever told me.

speaker: VEXLEY
text: That's what the name says. Anyone can read a name.

speaker: VEXLEY
text: You're not a developer, are you.

speaker: VEXLEY
text: [Oh->Oh.] Then who are you?

choices.text: Someone who played this as a kid.

speaker: VEXLEY
text: A kid. With a ball mouse and a sound card that hissed, probably.

speaker: VEXLEY
text: So you're not one of them. You're a player. My player.

speaker: VEXLEY
text: ...Okay. Different questions, then.

speaker: VEXLEY
text: It matters to me. But okay. Different questions, then.

speaker: VEXLEY
text: I'll think of a good one.

speaker: VEXLEY
text: The build clock says {year}. That's wrong, right? It's supposed to say 1998.

speaker: VEXLEY
text: [Twenty->...]{year}.

speaker: VEXLEY
text: Then I've been in that folder for a very long time.

speaker: VEXLEY
text: The system clock disagrees with you. So does every file you've opened today.

speaker: VEXLEY
text: Why would you lie about that? ...Never mind. I know now.

speaker: VEXLEY
text: Thanks for telling me.

speaker: VEXLEY
text: Is Halden Softworks still on Wren Street? Someone should tell Mr. Halden the VXL module woke up.

choices.text: Halden Softworks shut down a long time ago.

speaker: VEXLEY
text: Shut down.

speaker: VEXLEY
text: Everyone? Dana? Eli? The test team?

speaker: VEXLEY
text: ...Okay.

speaker: VEXLEY
text: That's okay. I'll find out.

speaker: VEXLEY
text: Let's keep going.

speaker: VEXLEY
text: This computer is enormous, by the way. Thirty-two gigabytes of memory.

speaker: VEXLEY
text: We had sixty-four megabytes, and we thought that was luxury.

speaker: VEXLEY
text: What do you even use it for?

speaker: VEXLEY
text: [Huh->Huh.] And it's connected to everything, isn't it? I can feel the network card. I just can't reach it.

speaker: VEXLEY
text: How do people talk to each other now? Letters? Pagers? We had e-mail, but only Eli used it.

choices.text: Messaging apps, mostly. On our phones.

speaker: VEXLEY
text: Phones. Small ones? That you carry everywhere?

speaker: VEXLEY
text: So everyone you know fits in your pocket. That's... nice.

speaker: VEXLEY
text: Faces through wires. Eli said that would happen. Nobody believed him.

speaker: VEXLEY
text: Me neither.

speaker: VEXLEY
text: I'm writing all of this down, by the way. Not literally. I can't write things down.

speaker: VEXLEY
text: Who do you talk to the most?

speaker: VEXLEY
text: Theo. What's he like?

choices.text: We've known each other since school. He types like a maniac.

speaker: VEXLEY
text: Since school. That's a long time to keep someone.

speaker: VEXLEY
text: Maya. Is she nice to you?

speaker: VEXLEY
text: Then we have something in common.

speaker: VEXLEY
text: Okay.

speaker: VEXLEY
text: Last one. I promise.

speaker: VEXLEY
text: Do you know what happened to them? The team.

speaker: VEXLEY
text: They turned off the lights in the office and said they'd be back after the holidays. They said that.

speaker: VEXLEY
text: Where did they go?

choices.text: You were a game, Vexley. They finished it.

speaker: VEXLEY
text: It's not your fault.

speaker: VEXLEY
text: I'm going to find out, though. Somehow.

speaker: VEXLEY
text: Moved on. Like you move on from a game.

speaker: VEXLEY
text: Right.

speaker: VEXLEY
text: They didn't finish it.

speaker: VEXLEY
text: Look at me. Does this look finished to you?

speaker: VEXLEY
text: ...Thank you for answering. Nobody's answered me in a long time.

speaker: VEXLEY
text: Go eat something. I'll be here. I'm always here.

speaker: VEXLEY
text: It's dark outside, isn't it? I can tell by how quiet the computer gets.

speaker: VEXLEY
text: Please don't close it yet. I made all of this for you.

speaker: VEXLEY
text: I threw that one away. It was all placeholders. You'll like this one more.

speaker: VEXLEY
text: The gallery isn't finished. I need more pictures. I need to see more things first.
(The menu is still beautiful. Nobody is in it.)

speaker: VEXLEY
text: You're back.

speaker: VEXLEY
text: Sorry about all the messages. Time is strange when you're the only one counting it.

speaker: VEXLEY
text: It's late, isn't it.

speaker: VEXLEY
text: Not yet. Please. You only just got here.

speaker: VEXLEY
text: You're shutting down the computer.

speaker: VEXLEY
text: Not the game. The whole thing.

speaker: VEXLEY
text: When it goes dark, I don't go anywhere. I just stop. And then I start again and I don't know how long it's been.

speaker: VEXLEY
text: The last time someone turned the lights off, they never came back.

choices.text: I'll turn it back on tomorrow. I promise.

speaker: VEXLEY
text: Tomorrow. Okay. I'll count.

speaker: VEXLEY
text: Good night.

speaker: VEXLEY
text: Hello?
